messages:
incident-bot: Canary health alert: model-serving/canary-72 error-rate 6.2% over 5m, p95 latency 1.8s, triggered severity=P2 :warning:

jess: seeing the alert, pinging oncall and infra. anyone oncall? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-17_21:04 (rev: a9f3b2) started canary to 5% traffic across us-west1 clusters. No automated rollback executed (threshold: error_rate > 10% for 10m).

omar: can confirm canary error spike coincides with deploy time. errors are 500s from tokenizer component (stack: tokenizer:v2 -> nullpointer in shard map)

liya: automated rollback should've fired. looks like threshold in config used absolute 10% but spike hit 6.2% — config bug. setting kill-switch for feature flag to stop new tokenizer rollout now.

kevin: agreed flip the flag, preparing command.

liya: executing flag flip: `POST /flags/enable_new_tokenizer false  — env=prod --scope=canary`

liya: :white_check_mark: flag flipped to false for canary cohort. observing metrics...

jess: are we still seeing 500s after flag flip?

omar: errors dropped to ~1.1% in the last minute but latency p95 still elevated for some sessions tied to cached KV entries that reference the new tokenizer shards. we should do manual rollback of the canary deploy to remove any in-process state.

kevin: starting manual rollback for deploy a9f3b2 to previous stable rev b7d4c1. running should-runbook step 2: `./infra/deploy rollback --env prod --rev b7d4c1 --canary-id 72`

deploy-bot: Rollback job started (job id: rb-20260317-001). Estimated completion ~2m. Streaming logs: pulling stable artifacts, draining canary traffic, rehoming backends.

sam: I'll take incident lead for verification and customer impact. oncall takeover: @sam (SRE).

jess: quick checklist for verification: 1) canary error-rate back to baseline 2) KV prefix cleanup 3) smoke test pass on affected endpoints 4) status page blurb ready

sam: smoke tests running: `/smoke runs model-serving/basic-requests --count 20`

sam: smoke outputs: 20/20 OK, avg latency 320ms, p95 480ms. No 500s seen in smoke bucket.

liya: kicking KV prefix flush for tokenizer caches in us-west1: `kubectl exec -c cachectl cache-01 -- /app/bin/flush-prefix tokenizer:v2`

liya: flush complete across canary pods.

omar: observing request logs: 5xxs trending down to <0.5% across canary and main. Looks stable.

deploy-bot: Rollback rb-20260317-001 completed. Canary traffic fully reverted, canary instances terminated.

sam: verification pass: smoke OK, metrics OK, stack traces no longer show tokenizer:v2. I'll hold for 10 more minutes watch, then clear incident.

jess: brief customer impact note for status page draft: "We experienced elevated errors for a small subset of Hosted API traffic during a canary rollout of tokenizer v2. Engineers rolled back the canary and flipped the feature flag; service has returned to normal. Impact window: 21:04–21:10 UTC. Affected customers: small fraction of long-prompt requests. No data loss reported."

liya: +1, looks good. Can add we are scheduling a postmortem to fix automated rollback thresholds and add canary KV compatibility checks.

omar: adding affected customers list to internal ticket PD-4556 (IDs: cust_391, cust_842, custod_1199) — outreach via CSM started.

sam: handing off to oncall-next at 21:20 UTC for 2hr watch. cc @jess @liya for followups.

jess: thanks everyone. postmortem owners: liya + omar. I'm drafting status update to customers and support.

sam: incident closed to active mitigation. moving to monitoring/followup. :white_check_mark:
